title: A volcano has erupted remnants of Earth's primordial magma ocean
description: Earth was once covered by a global magma ocean, which later cooled and crystallised – now traces of this primordial event have been found in magma from a young volcano in the Indian Ocean
author: Christa Lesté-Lasserre

title: Audacious mission to rescue NASA's falling telescope has launched
description: NASA’s Swift space telescope is reaching the end of its two-decade run in orbit – unless a satellite launched on 3 July can give it a lifesaving boost
author: Leah Crane

title: Orangutan mothers seem to plan playdates for their offspring
description: Female orangutans are generally solitary, but they travel more and eat less in an apparent effort to ensure their offspring have someone to play with
author: Chris Simms

title: June heatwave may have killed around 20,000 people in Europe
description: It will be some months before the true toll of Europe's worst-ever heatwave is confirmed, but researchers can estimate a death count based on how many people died in Europe during previous hot periods
author: Michael Le Page

title: Random wobbles in time could finally solve gravity’s greatest mystery
description: The question of how gravity interacts with the quantum world has long perplexed physicists, but a non-quantum theory of space-time could present an answer
author: Leah Crane

title: Geoengineering could expose plane passengers to sulphuric acid
description: A proposed technique to counter global warming by spraying sun-reflecting particles near the poles would cause commercial flights to pass through clouds of sulphuric acid, posing a danger to passengers and crew
author: Syris Valentine
